findings.what: ParamSpec labels reuse unrelated catalogue keys: ringing is 'Threshold', tape_speed is 'Quality', chroma_lowpass is 'Pre-blur', chroma_phase_noise is 'Corruptions', luma_smear is 'Radius'.
findings.why: If a UI renders these labels, they mislead the user. The card cannot add keys to the shared catalogue it does not own, so this is accepted as E1 and does not block the card. It does undercut the §16 usability intent.
findings.fix: Open a follow-up card on the catalogue owner to add NTSC-specific keys, then switch the labels. No change is needed in this diff.

findings.what: LABEL_NOTES is never read by the code. Its only consumer is a test that asserts its keys equal the parameter ids.
findings.why: It is dead data in the shipped module, and the test restates the declaration rather than checking behaviour.
findings.fix: Move it to a comment or docstring, or drop it together with the last test.

findings.what: `constant_k` is implemented as an ideal brick-wall filter (hard frequency cut). A real constant-k filter has a gradual rolloff with a peak near the cutoff.
findings.why: The name does not match the maths. The behaviour is still distinct from `butterworth` and does ring, so the acceptance items hold.
findings.fix: Rename the docstring and comment to say 'brick-wall approximation', or model an actual constant-k response.

findings.what: tracking_noise draws an independent uniform shift per line, up to 25 % of the width at 1.0. The VHS Home preset at 0.7 shifts lines by up to about 17 % of the width, and Glitch Tape at 0.9 by about 22 %.
findings.why: This tears the picture apart instead of giving a VHS-like wobble. The presets pass their distinctness tests but may look destructive by default. L17 is not a product-quality card, so this does not block.
findings.fix: Lower the preset values, or make the jitter low-frequency (correlated between neighbouring lines). A later card can tune this.

regression: none — the only change to existing code is one import line in effects/__init__.py, which registers the new 'ntsc' effect. No existing behaviour is altered and G7 is green.
renderer_invariants: all six hold (not applicable: this is an effect, not a CellRenderer; the input is copied by _copy, never mutated, and a test checks it)
notes:
Read from the diff only; I did not run the tests, and the gate results come from the card. I checked the six accept items against the code and they hold: neutral is the identity, the head-switching band is bounded and parameterised, chroma low-pass touches only I and Q, the six presets are distinct, simple mode has exactly 4 parameters, and shape is preserved.
The earlier pass-1 and pass-2 findings are fixed in the code: bandwidth runs along axis 1, the ringing kernel has lobes, the head-switching shift is clamped, the rng argument and the seed parameter both drive the noise, and each stochastic stage has its own child generator.
No abstraction leak and no host coupling: the module imports only the registry and types.
The label problem needs a catalogue-owning card, so it is a follow-up and not a blocker for this one.
